mainTopic: Dreams follow their interpretation: the story of בַּר הֶדְיָא, אַבָּיֵי and רָבָא
overview: The amud opens with two rulers who ask Jewish sages to predict their dreams. Each ruler thinks all day about the frightening image he was given, and he dreams it that night. The גמרא then tells about בַּר הֶדְיָא, a dream interpreter who gave good readings to clients who paid and bad readings to those who did not. אַבָּיֵי paid him and רָבָא did not, so the very same dreams were read as success for אַבָּיֵי and as disaster for רָבָא. Several of רָבָא's bad readings come true, including his arrest and two blows from a club. Once רָבָא pays, his readings turn good. רָבָא then finds a book that says all dreams follow the interpretation, so he holds בַּר הֶדְיָא responsible and curses him. בַּר הֶדְיָא flees into exile in Rome, where his habit of demanding a זוז gets him blamed for ruining the king's silks; the story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The emperor asks what he will dream
steps.stepSummary: The emperor tests רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּרַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא by asking him to predict a dream.
steps.simpleTranslation: The emperor says: You claim to be very wise. Tell me what I will see in my dream.
steps.whatsHappening: The emperor poses a challenge. This sets up the answer and the dream that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He asks about a future dream, not one he has already had. That timing matters because the answer can occupy his thoughts before he sleeps.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ קֵיסָר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּרַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא:
phrases.english: The emperor said to Rabbi Yehoshua son of Rabbi Ḥananya:
You say that you are very wise,
tell me what I will see in my dream.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ קֵיסָר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּרַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the emperor will see in a future dream.

steps.title: A vivid prediction becomes the dream
steps.stepSummary: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּרַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא supplies frightening images; the emperor thinks about them all day and dreams them that night.
steps.simpleTranslation: He tells the emperor that Persians will capture and enslave him and make him herd unclean animals with a golden staff. The emperor thinks about it all day and sees it that night.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer gives the emperor a specific image to picture. The account then reports that he thinks about it all day and dreams it that night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daytime thought links the prediction to the later dream. The account does not say that the predicted capture actually happened.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חָזֵית דִּמְשַׁחֲרִי לָךְ פָּרְסָאֵי
phrases.english: He said to him: You will see Persians capture you
and enslave you, and make you herd unclean animals
with a golden staff.
He thought about it the entire day,
and that night he saw it in a dream.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חָזֵית דִּמְשַׁחֲרִי לָךְ פָּרְסָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the emperor’s question and reports what happened afterward.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A detailed dream image, which the emperor later dreams.

steps.title: שַׁבּוּר מַלְכָּא asks the same kind of question
steps.stepSummary: שַׁבּוּר מַלְכָּא asks שְׁמוּאֵל to predict his dream.
steps.simpleTranslation: שַׁבּוּר מַלְכָּא says to שְׁמוּאֵל: You claim to be very wise. Tell me what I will see in my dream.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ruler asks the same kind of question. This sets up a parallel example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording closely follows the emperor’s question. The second account will show whether the same sequence occurs again.

phrases.english: King Shapur said to Shmuel:
You say that you are very wise,
tell me what I will see in my dream.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שַׁבּוּר מַלְכָּא, לִשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a parallel account with a different ruler and sage.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What King Shapur will see in a future dream.

steps.title: The second ruler dreams what he contemplated
steps.stepSummary: שְׁמוּאֵל describes Roman captors and a golden mill; שַׁבּוּר מַלְכָּא thinks about it all day and dreams it.
steps.simpleTranslation: שְׁמוּאֵל says that Romans will capture the king and make him grind date pits in a golden mill. The king thinks about it all day and sees it that night.
steps.whatsHappening: שְׁמוּאֵל answers with another vivid scene. The account again connects a full day of thought to that night’s dream.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The feared captors change from Persians to Romans, but the sequence stays the same. The reported result is the dream, not an actual capture.

phrases.english: He said to him: You will see Romans come
and capture you,
and make you grind date pits in a golden mill.
He thought about it the entire day,
and that night he saw it in a dream.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חָזֵית דְּאָתוּ רוֹמָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers King Shapur’s question and completes the parallel account.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A detailed dream image, which the king later dreams.

steps.title: The interpreter’s payment rule
steps.stepSummary: בַּר הֶדְיָא interprets dreams favorably for paying clients and unfavorably for nonpaying clients; אַבָּיֵי pays, while רָבָא does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: בַּר הֶדְיָא interpreted dreams. He gave favorable interpretations to those who paid and unfavorable ones to those who did not. אַבָּיֵי paid him a coin; רָבָא did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The account introduces a dream interpreter and his practice. It then identifies who pays, setting up the contrasting interpretations below.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The payment detail explains why the two men will receive different readings. Keep that detail in mind even when they report the same dream text.

phrases.english: Bar Haddaya was an interpreter of dreams.

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּיָהֵיב לֵיהּ אַגְרָא — מְפַשַּׁר לֵיהּ לִמְעַלְּיוּתָא,
phrases.english: For one who paid him, he interpreted favorably,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן דְּלָא יָהֵיב לֵיהּ אַגְרָא — מְפַשַּׁר לֵיהּ לִגְרִיעוּתָא.
phrases.english: and for one who did not pay him, he interpreted unfavorably.
Abaye and Rava saw a dream.
Abaye gave him a coin,
but Rava did not pay him.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּר הֶדְיָא מְפַשַּׁר חֶלְמֵי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from predictions of future dreams to interpretations of dreams already seen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בַּר הֶדְיָא’s favorable or unfavorable interpretation depends on whether he receives payment.

steps.title: One verse receives opposite business readings
steps.stepSummary: The same dream verse becomes business loss for רָבָא and business profit for אַבָּיֵי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They report hearing, “Your ox shall be slaughtered before your eyes.” בַּר הֶדְיָא tells רָבָא that business loss will leave him too sad to eat. He tells אַבָּיֵי that business profit will leave him too joyful to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The two men report the same verse from their dreams. בַּר הֶדְיָא gives each a different reason for being unable to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רָבָא, sorrow follows loss; for אַבָּיֵי, joy follows profit. This is the first example of the payment pattern just described.

keyTerms.meaning: your business will suffer a loss

phrases.english: They said to him: We were read in our dreams
“Your ox shall be slaughtered before your eyes, etc.”
To Rava he said: Your business will suffer a loss
and you will be unable to enjoy eating
because of the sadness in your heart.
To Abaye he said: Your business will profit
and you will be unable to enjoy eating
because of the joy in your heart.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: אַקְרִינַן בְּחֶלְמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first concrete example of the payment rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בַּר הֶדְיָא reads the same dream verse favorably for אַבָּיֵי and unfavorably for רָבָא.

steps.title: A second verse is read literally or favorably
steps.stepSummary: בַּר הֶדְיָא gives רָבָא the verse’s adverse sense, but tells אַבָּיֵי that numerous daughters will marry and leave home.
steps.simpleTranslation: They report hearing a verse about bearing sons and daughters. He gives רָבָא its plain adverse meaning. To אַבָּיֵי, he predicts many children; his daughters’ marriages will merely feel like their being taken away.
steps.whatsHappening: The two men bring another dream verse. בַּר הֶדְיָא again gives them sharply different readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רָבָא receives the verse’s threatening sense. For אַבָּיֵי, the feeling of losing daughters comes from their marriages, not captivity.

keyTerms.meaning: you will bear sons and daughters

phrases.english: They said to him: We were read
“You shall bear sons and daughters, etc.”
To Rava he said: It means its plain, adverse sense.

phrases.aramaic: לְאַבָּיֵי אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּנָךְ וּבְנָתָךְ נְפִישִׁי,
phrases.english: To Abaye he said: Your sons and daughters will be numerous,
and your daughters will marry people outside your household,
and it will seem to you as though they are going into captivity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: אַקְרִינַן ״בָּנִים וּבָנוֹת תּוֹלִיד וְגוֹ׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the contrast using a different verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The unfavorable reading follows the verse’s adverse sense; the favorable reading treats separation through marriage as the experience described.

steps.title: “Another people” receives two family readings
steps.stepSummary: For אַבָּיֵי, the words refer to his wife’s relatives; for רָבָא, they refer to a woman caring for his children after his wife’s death.
steps.simpleTranslation: They hear, “Your sons and daughters are given to another people.” בַּר הֶדְיָא tells אַבָּיֵי that his wife will prevail in choosing her relatives as spouses for their children. He tells רָבָא that his wife will die and their children will come into another woman’s care.
steps.whatsHappening: A third dream verse says that children are given to “another people.” בַּר הֶדְיָא applies that phrase differently to each man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אַבָּיֵי, “another” means relatives on his wife’s side rather than his own. For רָבָא, it means a woman who will take charge of the children after their mother dies.

phrases.english: They were read: “Your sons and daughters are given to another people.”

phrases.aramaic: לְאַבָּיֵי אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּנָךְ וּבְנָתָךְ נְפִישִׁין,
phrases.english: To Abaye he said: Your sons and daughters will be numerous,

phrases.aramaic: אַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ לְקָרִיבָךְ וְהִיא אָמְרָה לְקָרִיבַהּ,
phrases.english: you will say they should marry your relatives, and she will say her relatives,
and she will prevail over you and give them to her relatives,
who will be like another people to you.
To Rava he said: Your wife will die,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָתוּ בְּנֵיהּ וּבְנָתֵיהּ לִידֵי אִיתְּתָא אַחֲרִיתִי.
phrases.english: and his sons and daughters will come into another woman’s care.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַקְרְיֻין ״בָּנֶיךָ וּבְנֹתֶיךָ נְתֻנִים לְעַם אַחֵר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third pair of contrasting interpretations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The same phrase, “another people,” is applied favorably to אַבָּיֵי and painfully to רָבָא.

steps.title: An earlier teaching explains the stepmother reading
steps.stepSummary: A teaching cited by רָבָא identifies the verse’s “another people” with אֵשֶׁת הָאָב, supporting the preceding reading about another woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רָבָא cites רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא citing רַב: What does “Your sons and daughters are given to another people” mean? It refers to the father’s wife—the children’s stepmother.
steps.whatsHappening: The account now supplies a teaching about the verse. It explains why the preceding interpretation speaks of children coming into another woman’s care.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אֵשֶׁת הָאָב means the father’s wife, who is the children’s stepmother. The citation supports that reading of “another people”; it does not add a new dream.

keyTerms.meaning: what does the written verse mean?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: For Rava said that Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״בָּנֶיךָ וּבְנֹתֶיךָ נְתֻנִים לְעַם אַחֵר״ —
phrases.english: What is meant by the verse, “Your sons and daughters are given to another people”?
This refers to the father’s wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a cited interpretation of the verse used in the reading given to רָבָא.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that children may come under the care of their father’s new wife.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching transmitted by רָבָא in the name of רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא in the name of רַב.

steps.title: Eating with joy—or trying to calm fear
steps.stepSummary: בַּר הֶדְיָא gives אַבָּיֵי and רָבָא opposite readings of a joyful verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: They dreamed that a verse about eating bread with joy was read to them. בַּר הֶדְיָא tells אַבָּיֵי that his business will prosper and he will recite the verse happily. He tells רָבָא that his business will fail; he will slaughter food but not eat it, and will recite the verse to calm his fear.
steps.whatsHappening: The two men report the same dream verse. בַּר הֶדְיָא makes its words describe joy for אַבָּיֵי but distress for רָבָא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אַבָּיֵי, eating and reciting follow business success. For רָבָא, the food is prepared but not eaten, and reciting serves to ease fear rather than express happiness.

keyTerms.meaning: from the joy of your heart

phrases.english: It was read to us in a dream: “Go, eat your bread with joy.”
To Abaye he said: Your business will profit,
and you will eat and drink and recite the verse
from the joy of your heart.
To Rava he said: Your business will suffer a loss,
you will slaughter but not eat, and you will drink
and recite it to ease your fear.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַקְרִינַן בְּחֶלְמִין: ״לֵךְ אֱכֹל בְּשִׂמְחָה לַחְמֶךָ״.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the reading about another woman, the account moves to a new shared dream verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The same joyful words are applied to אַבָּיֵי as genuine joy and to רָבָא as an attempt to manage fear.

steps.title: Reading the beginning for one person and the end for the other
steps.stepSummary: For two more dream verses, בַּר הֶדְיָא uses the beginning for אַבָּיֵי and the ending for רָבָא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They dreamed of a verse beginning, “You will bring much seed into the field.” בַּר הֶדְיָא interpreted its beginning for אַבָּיֵי and its ending for רָבָא. He did the same with a verse beginning, “You will have olive trees throughout your borders.”
steps.whatsHappening: The account gives two short examples of the same method. For each verse, בַּר הֶדְיָא chooses its beginning for אַבָּיֵי and its ending for רָבָא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spoken opening of each verse sounds promising. Its unquoted ending supplies the bad outcome for רָבָא; the text marks the contrast without repeating those endings.

phrases.english: It was read to us: “You will bring much seed into the field.”
To Abaye he interpreted it from its beginning;
to Rava he interpreted it from its end.

phrases.aramaic: אַקְרִינַן ״זֵיתִים יִהְיוּ לְךָ בְּכׇל גְּבוּלֶךָ וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: It was read to us: “You will have olive trees throughout all your borders, etc.”
To Abaye he interpreted it from its beginning;
to Rava he interpreted it from its end.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַקְרִינַן ״זֶרַע רַב תּוֹצִיא הַשָּׂדֶה״.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite readings continue, now by selecting different parts of each verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בַּר הֶדְיָא takes the promising beginning for אַבָּיֵי and the harmful ending for רָבָא in both examples.

steps.title: Being feared can mean honor or suspicion
steps.stepSummary: בַּר הֶדְיָא reads a verse about public fear as honor for אַבָּיֵי and arrest for רָבָא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They dreamed of the verse beginning, “All the peoples of the earth will see.” בַּר הֶדְיָא tells אַבָּיֵי that he will become known as head of the academy and people will fear him. He tells רָבָא that the king’s treasury will be broken into, רָבָא will be seized as a suspected thief, and everyone will draw an inference from his case.
steps.whatsHappening: בַּר הֶדְיָא again gives opposite meanings to one dream verse. He makes public fear a sign of standing for אַבָּיֵי, but a result of suspected theft for רָבָא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אַבָּיֵי, people hear his name and regard him with awe. For רָבָא, an arrest makes people compare their own situation to his through a קַל וָחוֹמֶר.

keyTerms.meaning: an inference from one case to a stronger case

phrases.english: It was read to us: “And all the peoples of the earth will see, etc.”

phrases.aramaic: לְאַבָּיֵי אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נָפֵק לָךְ שְׁמָא
phrases.english: To Abaye he said: Your name will become known

phrases.aramaic: דְּרֵישׁ מְתִיבְתָּא הָוֵית, אֵימְתָךְ נְפַלַת בְּעָלְמָא.
phrases.english: as head of the academy; fear of you will fall upon the world.

phrases.aramaic: לְרָבָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בֵּדַיְינָא דְּמַלְכָּא אִתְּבַר,
phrases.english: To Rava he said: The king’s treasury will be broken into,
and you will be seized among the thieves,

phrases.aramaic: וְדָיְינִי כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא קַל וָחוֹמֶר מִינָּךְ.
phrases.english: and everyone will draw an a fortiori inference from you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַקְרִינַן ״וְרָאוּ כׇּל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ וְגוֹ׳״.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The contrasting interpretations continue with a new verse, now focused on how other people react.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בַּר הֶדְיָא interprets public fear as honor for אַבָּיֵי and as part of a theft accusation for רָבָא.

steps.title: The predicted arrest takes place
steps.stepSummary: The next day, the king’s treasury is broken into and רָבָא is seized.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next day, the king’s treasury was broken into, and people came and seized רָבָא.
steps.whatsHappening: The account reports what happened the next day. The break-in and רָבָא’s arrest match the prediction just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a reported event, not another interpretation of the verse. It confirms the specific unfavorable outcome that בַּר הֶדְיָא described for רָבָא.

phrases.english: The next day, the king’s treasury was broken into,
and they came and seized Rava.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִמְחַר אִתְּבַר בֵּדַיְינָא דְּמַלְכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The narrative moves from בַּר הֶדְיָא’s prediction to an event matching it.
steps.raayaObject: The prediction that the king’s treasury would be broken into and רָבָא would be seized.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The account’s report of the next day’s break-in and arrest.
steps.whatToRemember: The last example does more than give two readings: it also reports the event that followed רָבָא’s reading.

steps.title: Lettuce on the barrels
steps.stepSummary: They dreamed of lettuce on the mouth of the barrels. בר הדיא told אביי his business will spread out like lettuce, and told רבא his business will be bitter like lettuce.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We saw lettuce on the mouth of the barrels. To אביי he said: Your business will double like lettuce. To רבא he said: Your business will be bitter like lettuce.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי and רבא tell בר הדיא the same dream about lettuce, and he gives them opposite meanings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lettuce has two sides: its leaves are wide and full, but its stalk is bitter. בר הדיא picks the good side (growth) for אביי and the bad side (bitterness) for רבא. This is the same pattern as the earlier steps: one image, two opposite readings.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: חֲזַן חַסָּא עַל פּוּם דַּנֵּי.
phrases.english: They said to him: We saw lettuce on the mouth of the barrels.
phrases.notes: Both אביי and רבא report the same dream.

phrases.english: To Abaye he said:
Your business will double like lettuce.
phrases.notes: Lettuce leaves are wide and plentiful, a sign of growth.

phrases.english: To Rava he said:
Your business will be bitter like lettuce.
phrases.notes: Lettuce stalk is bitter, a sign of a bad outcome.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: חֲזַן חַסָּא עַל פּוּם דַּנֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story jumped ahead to רבא's arrest, the גמרא returns to listing more dream readings by בר הדיא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The same lettuce image means growth for אביי and bitterness for רבא.

steps.title: Meat on the barrels
steps.stepSummary: They dreamed of meat on the barrels. For אביי, his wine will be sweet and people will buy meat and wine from him; for רבא, his wine will turn sour and people will buy meat to dip in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We saw meat on the mouth of the barrels. To אביי he said: Your wine will be sweet, and everyone will come to buy meat and wine from you. To רבא he said: Your wine will turn sharp (sour), and everyone will come to buy meat to eat with it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second dream image, meat on the barrels, again gets a happy reading for אביי and a sad one for רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both readings people come to buy from them, but for different reasons. For אביי they want his good wine together with meat. For רבא the wine has become vinegar, so people only want it as a dip for their meat, which means a cheap sale and a loss.

keyTerms.meaning: Sharp, i.e. turned sour into vinegar

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: חֲזַן בִּשְׂרָא עַל פּוּם דַּנֵּי.
phrases.english: They said to him: We saw meat on the mouth of the barrels.
To Abaye he said: Your wine will be sweet,
and everyone will come
to buy meat and wine from you.
To Rava he said: Your wine will turn sour,
and everyone will come
to buy meat to eat with it.
phrases.notes: They will dip their meat in רבא's vinegar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: חֲזַן בִּשְׂרָא עַל פּוּם דַּנֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second wine-barrel dream with the same good-versus-bad pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat on the barrels means sweet, selling wine for אביי and soured wine for רבא.

steps.title: A barrel hanging on a palm tree
steps.stepSummary: They dreamed of a barrel hanging from a palm tree. For אביי, his business will rise high like a palm; for רבא, his goods will be sweet (cheap) like dates.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We saw a barrel hanging on a palm tree. To אביי he said: Your business will rise like a palm tree. To רבא he said: Your business will be sweet like dates.
steps.whatsHappening: A third dream, a barrel on a palm tree, is read as rising success for אביי and as cheap prices for רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again בר הדיא chooses two different features of the palm. For אביי he uses the tree's height, meaning his business goes up. For רבא he uses the dates, which were very cheap in בבל, so 'sweet like dates' really means he will have to sell for almost nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Will be raised up, will rise

steps.confusionAlert: 'Sweet like dates' sounds like a blessing, but it is the bad reading: dates were so cheap in בבל that it means רבא will sell his goods at a very low price.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: חֲזַן חָבִיתָא דִּתְלֵי בְּדִיקְלָא.
phrases.english: They said to him: We saw a barrel hanging on a palm tree.

phrases.aramaic: לְאַבָּיֵי אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִדְּלֵי עִסְקָךְ כְּדִיקְלָא.
phrases.english: To Abaye he said: Your business will rise like a palm tree.

phrases.aramaic: לְרָבָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲלֵי עִסְקָךְ כְּתַמְרֵי.
phrases.english: To Rava he said: Your business will be sweet like dates.
phrases.notes: Dates were cheap, so his goods will sell cheaply.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: חֲזַן חָבִיתָא דִּתְלֵי בְּדִיקְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third dream image in the same list, continuing the identical pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The palm tree means rising business for אביי and cheap selling for רבא.

steps.title: A pomegranate sprouting on the barrels
steps.stepSummary: They dreamed of a pomegranate sprouting on the barrels. For אביי, his business will gain value like a pomegranate; for רבא, it will go sour like a pomegranate.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We saw a pomegranate sprouting on the mouth of the barrels. To אביי he said: Your business will be valuable like a pomegranate. To רבא he said: Your business will go sour like a pomegranate.
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth dream, a pomegranate on the barrels, again brings gain for אביי and loss for רבא, finishing this set of barrel dreams.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pomegranate is full and valuable, but it can also be sour. בר הדיא gives אביי the value and gives רבא the sourness. Four times in a row, the same dream gets opposite readings, showing that his answers depended on who paid him.
steps.whatToRemember: In all four barrel dreams (lettuce, meat, palm tree, pomegranate), אביי and רבא saw exactly the same thing. The only difference was the interpretation בר הדיא chose, good for the one who paid and bad for the one who did not.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: חֲזַן רוּמָּנָא דְּקָדְחָא אַפּוּם דַּנֵּי,
phrases.english: They said to him: We saw a pomegranate sprouting on the mouth of the barrels,

phrases.aramaic: לְאַבָּיֵי אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עֲשִׁיק עִסְקָךְ כְּרוּמָּנָא.
phrases.english: To Abaye he said: Your business will increase in value like a pomegranate.

phrases.aramaic: לְרָבָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ: קָאוֵי עִסְקָךְ כְּרוּמָּנָא.
phrases.english: To Rava he said: Your business will go sour like a pomegranate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: חֲזַן רוּמָּנָא דְּקָדְחָא אַפּוּם דַּנֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth and final barrel-related dream in this run, repeating the same opposite-reading pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pomegranate means increased value for אביי and souring for רבא.

steps.title: The barrel that fell into a pit
steps.stepSummary: Both dreamed a barrel fell into a pit. For אביי it means his goods will be in high demand; for רבא it means his goods will be ruined and thrown into a pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told him: We saw a barrel fall into a pit. To אביי he said: Your merchandise will be sought after, like the saying 'Bread fell into a pit and could not be found.' To רבא he said: Your merchandise will spoil and you will throw it into a pit.
steps.whatsHappening: Another shared dream is presented, and בר הדיא again gives אביי a good reading and רבא a bad one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, 'falling and disappearing' means his goods vanish because everyone buys them up. For רבא, the same image means his goods literally go to waste. The pattern of one picture with two opposite readings continues from Steps 14-17.

keyTerms.meaning: Your merchandise will be in demand

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: חֲזַן חָבִיתָא דִּנְפַל לְבֵירָא.
phrases.english: They said to him: We saw a barrel that fell into a pit.
To Abaye he said: Your merchandise will be in demand,
as people say: 'Bread fell into a pit and was not found.'
phrases.notes: It vanishes because everyone grabs it up.

phrases.english: To Rava he said: Your merchandise will be ruined
and you will throw it into a pit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: חֲזַן חָבִיתָא דִּנְפַל לְבֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next dream in the same series of paired interpretations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One dream image is read as success for אביי and as loss for רבא.

steps.title: The braying donkey foal
steps.stepSummary: They dreamed of a donkey foal braying by their heads. אביי will become head of a ישיבה with a speaker beside him; רבא is told the words 'פטר חמור' are erased from his תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told him: We saw a young donkey standing by our heads and braying. To אביי he said: You will be a king, and a speaker will stand by you. To רבא he said: The words 'פטר חמור' are erased from your תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: Another shared dream: אביי hears of greatness, and רבא hears that something is wrong with his תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, the braying is read as the אמורא who loudly repeats the head of the ישיבה's lesson to the crowd. For רבא, the donkey points to the verse about 'פטר חמור' in the parashah written inside תפילין. This sets up רבא's objection in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The speaker who repeats the teacher's words aloud to the audience
Firstborn donkey (a phrase in the תפילין parashah)

phrases.english: They said to him: We saw a donkey foal
standing by our heads and braying.
To Abaye he said: You will be a king,
phrases.notes: That is, head of the ישיבה.

phrases.english: and an interpreter will stand beside you.

phrases.aramaic: לְרָבָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר״ גְּהִיט מִתְּפִילָּךְ.
phrases.english: To Rava he said: 'Peter chamor' is erased from your tefillin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: חֲזֵינַן בַּר חֲמָרָא דְּקָאֵי אַאִיסָדַן וְנוֹעֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next paired dream. This time רבא's reading is a factual claim about his תפילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Donkey braying means leadership for אביי and a defect in the תפילין for רבא.

steps.title: רבא objects that the words are there
steps.stepSummary: רבא protests that he has seen his תפילין himself and the words are present.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רבא) said to him: I myself looked, and it is there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges בר הדיא's claim with his own eyewitness check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the business predictions, this claim can be checked right now. רבא says he saw the words 'פטר חמור' in his תפילין, which seems to prove the interpreter wrong.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְדִידִי חֲזֵי לִי וְאִיתֵיהּ.
phrases.english: He said to him: I myself saw it, and it is there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְדִידִי חֲזֵי לִי וְאִיתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading given to רבא in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר הדיא's claim that 'פטר חמור' is erased from רבא's תפילין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Direct observation: רבא checked and the words are written there.

steps.title: Only the letter ו is erased
steps.stepSummary: בר הדיא narrows his claim: the ו of 'חמור' is certainly erased.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The ו of 'פטר חמור' is certainly erased from your תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: בר הדיא answers רבא's objection by making his claim more precise. Only one letter is missing, not the whole phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא saw the phrase, but a single missing letter is easy to overlook. Even one missing letter makes תפילין invalid, so the warning still holds.
steps.confusionAlert: בר הדיא is not taking back his claim. He is pinpointing it: the phrase is visible, but one letter in it is gone.

phrases.english: He said to him: The vav of 'peter chamor'
is certainly erased from your tefillin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וָאו דְּ״פֶטֶר חֲמוֹר״ וַדַּאי גְּהִיט מִתְּפִילָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole phrase is missing, which רבא disproved by looking.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the ו is missing, a detail רבא could easily have missed.

steps.title: רבא alone: the fallen outer door
steps.stepSummary: רבא goes to בר הדיא by himself. He dreamed his outer door fell, and is told his wife will die.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end רבא went to him alone. He said: I saw the outer door fall. He said to him: Your wife will die.
steps.whatsHappening: The story shifts. רבא now visits alone, and the interpretations become even harsher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The door guards the house, and a wife is seen as the one who guards the home. So a fallen door is read as the loss of his wife. רבא still has not paid, which explains the bad readings.

phrases.english: Eventually Rava went to him alone.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזַאי דַּשָּׁא בָּרָיְיתָא דִּנְפַל.
phrases.english: He said to him: I saw the outer door fall.
He said to him: Your wife will die.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְסוֹף אֲזַל רָבָא לְחוֹדֵיהּ לְגַבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the paired dreams and begins רבא's private session.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fallen outer door means the wife's death.

steps.title: Teeth falling out
steps.stepSummary: רבא dreamed his molars and front teeth fell out, and is told his sons and daughters will die.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I saw my molars and teeth fall out. He said: Your sons and daughters will die.
steps.whatsHappening: Another of רבא's private dreams receives a frightening reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Teeth are part of a person, close to him and many in number, so they are read as one's children. Both kinds of teeth fall, matching both sons and daughters.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזַאי כַּכַּי וְשִׁנַּי דִּנְתוּר.
phrases.english: He said to him: I saw my back teeth and front teeth fall out.
He said to him: Your sons and daughters will die.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזַאי כַּכַּי וְשִׁנַּי דִּנְתוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next private dream in the same session.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fallen teeth mean the death of one's children.

steps.title: Two doves flying away
steps.stepSummary: רבא dreamed two doves flew off, and is told he will divorce two wives.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I saw two doves flying. He said: You will divorce two women.
steps.whatsHappening: A third private dream gets another bad reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doves often symbolize a wife or mate. Two doves flying away means two women leaving him through divorce.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזַאי תַּרְתֵּי יוֹנֵי דְּפָרְחָן.
phrases.english: He said to him: I saw two doves that were flying.
He said to him: You will divorce two women.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזַאי תַּרְתֵּי יוֹנֵי דְּפָרְחָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next private dream.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two flying doves mean two divorces.

steps.title: Two turnip heads
steps.stepSummary: רבא dreamed of two turnip heads, and is told he will be struck with a club twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I saw two turnip heads. He said: You will take two blows from a club.
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth private dream is read as two beatings. This sets up the very next scene, where it comes true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A turnip head is round and heavy like the knob of a club. Two turnips means exactly two blows, and that exact number matters in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: You will 'swallow', meaning take or receive

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזַאי תְּרֵי גַּרְגְּלִידֵי דְלִפְתָּא.
phrases.english: He said to him: I saw two turnip heads.
He said to him: You will receive two blows of a club.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזַאי תְּרֵי גַּרְגְּלִידֵי דְלִפְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Last of the four private dreams before payment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two turnip heads mean two blows.

steps.title: The two blows come true that day
steps.stepSummary: רבא spends the day in the בית מדרש to stay safe. He tries to separate two blind men who are fighting and is struck twice. When they raise their sticks again, he says, 'Enough, I only saw two.'
steps.simpleTranslation: That day רבא went and sat in the בית מדרש all day. He found two blind men fighting with each other. רבא went to separate them, and they hit רבא twice. When they raised their sticks to hit him again, he said: Enough! I only saw two.
steps.whatsHappening: The story shows the turnip-head reading from Step 25 coming true exactly, even though רבא tried to avoid it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא hid in the safest place, the בית מדרש, yet the beating found him there. He trusts the dream's exact number so fully that he stops the third blow by saying the dream showed only two. This supports the idea from earlier in the sugya that the interpretation decides the dream's outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: Blind people (literally: 'with much light', a polite expression)

steps.whatToRemember: The bad reading of the unpaid interpreter came true to the exact detail, two blows and no more. That shows how much power the interpretation has.
steps.confusionAlert: 'סגי נהורי' literally means 'much light', but it is a polite way of saying 'blind'. The men were not seeing well.

phrases.english: That day Rava went
and sat in the study hall the whole day.
He found these two blind men
who were fighting with each other.
Rava went to separate them,
and they struck Rava two blows.
They raised their sticks to strike him another,
he said: Enough for me, I saw only two.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל רָבָא הָהוּא יוֹמָא וִיתֵיב בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא כּוּלֵּיהּ יוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the reading of Step 25 being fulfilled.
steps.raayaObject: That בר הדיא's interpretations come true exactly as spoken.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא receives exactly two blows the same day and avoids a third.

steps.title: רבא pays: the fallen wall
steps.stepSummary: רבא finally pays בר הדיא. He dreamed his wall fell, and is now told he will acquire property without boundaries.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end רבא came and gave him a fee. He said: I saw a wall fall. He said: You will acquire property without borders.
steps.whatsHappening: The story turns. Once רבא pays, the interpretations become good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fallen wall could easily be read as ruin, but now it means the boundary walls are gone, so his land has no limits. Payment is what changed, which confirms that the interpreter's words steer the outcome.
steps.whatToRemember: Before payment, every reading was bad. After payment, every reading is good. The interpretation, not the dream image, decides the result.

phrases.aramaic: לְסוֹף אֲתָא רָבָא וִיהֵיב לֵיהּ אַגְרָא.
phrases.english: Eventually Rava came and gave him a fee.
He said to him: I saw a wall fall.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נְכָסִים בְּלֹא מְצָרִים קָנֵית.
phrases.english: He said to him: You will acquire property without boundaries.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְסוֹף אֲתָא רָבָא וִיהֵיב לֵיהּ אַגְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the pattern of Steps 22-26 after payment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fallen wall means boundless property.

steps.title: אביי's house falls on רבא
steps.stepSummary: רבא dreamed אביי's house fell and its dust covered him. He is told אביי will die and his ישיבה will come to רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I saw אביי's palace fall, and its dust covered me. He said: אביי will die, and his ישיבה will come to you.
steps.whatsHappening: Another good reading for רבא, predicting that he will inherit אביי's position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dust 'covering' רבא means what was אביי's settles onto him. Historically, רבא did lead after אביי, so this fits.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזַאי אַפַּדְנָא דְּאַבָּיֵי דִּנְפַל
phrases.english: He said to him: I saw Abaye's house fall
and its dust covered me.
He said to him: Abaye will die
and his yeshiva will come to you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזַאי אַפַּדְנָא דְּאַבָּיֵי דִּנְפַל וְכַסְּיַין אַבְקֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next dream after payment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי's falling house means רבא inherits his ישיבה.

steps.title: Everyone takes רבא's bricks
steps.stepSummary: רבא dreamed his own house fell and everyone took the bricks. He is told his teachings will spread throughout the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I saw my palace fall, and everyone came and took brick after brick. He said: Your teachings will be scattered throughout the world.
steps.whatsHappening: Another good reading: people carrying off his bricks means people carrying his Torah everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each brick stands for one teaching. Everyone taking a piece means his teachings are spread and quoted far and wide.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזַאי אַפַּדְנָא דִידִי דִּנְפַל,
phrases.english: He said to him: I saw my own house fall,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲתוֹ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא שְׁקוּל לְבֵינְתָּא לְבֵינְתָּא.
phrases.english: and everyone came and took brick by brick.
He said to him: Your teachings will be spread throughout the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזַאי אַפַּדְנָא דִידִי דִּנְפַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next dream after payment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bricks being carried off means teachings being spread.

steps.title: Split head becomes a feather from the pillow
steps.stepSummary: רבא dreamed his head split and his brain fell out. He is told only that a feather will come out of his pillow.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I saw my head split open and my brain fall out. He said: A feather will come out of the pillow.
steps.whatsHappening: A terrifying dream is given a harmless reading now that רבא has paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something 'coming out from near the head' is shrunk to a feather slipping out of the pillow. Even a gruesome image can be read as trivial.

phrases.english: He said to him: I saw that my head split open
and my brain fell out.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אוּדְרָא מִבֵּי סָדְיָא נָפֵיק.
phrases.english: He said to him: A feather will come out of the pillow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזַאי דְּאִבְּקַע רֵישִׁי וּנְתַר מוּקְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next dream after payment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A split head means only a feather falling from the pillow.

steps.title: Hearing the Egyptian הלל
steps.stepSummary: רבא dreamed the Egyptian הלל was read to him. He is told miracles will happen for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: The Egyptian הלל was read to me in a dream. He said: Miracles will be done for you.
steps.whatsHappening: The last dream here gets a very positive reading. The story continues afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'Egyptian הלל' is the הלל that praises ה׳ for the miracles of leaving Egypt. Hearing it in a dream points to miracles in רבא's own life.

keyTerms.meaning: The Egyptian הלל (praise for the Exodus)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַקְרְיוּן הַלֵּלָא מִצְרָאָה בְּחֶלְמָא.
phrases.english: He said to him: They read me the Egyptian Hallel in a dream.
He said to him: Miracles will happen for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַקְרְיוּן הַלֵּלָא מִצְרָאָה בְּחֶלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next dream after payment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hearing the Egyptian הלל means miracles.

steps.title: בר הדיא fears traveling with רבא on a ship
steps.stepSummary: בר הדיא is on a ship with רבא. He worries about being near someone who has been promised miracles.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר הדיא was traveling with רבא on a ship. He said: Why do I need to be with a man for whom miracles happen?
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves to a new scene. בר הדיא and רבא are on a boat together, and בר הדיא gets nervous because of his own last interpretation for רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 31, בר הדיא told רבא that miracles would happen for him. Now בר הדיא fears what kind of miracle that might be. Perhaps the ship will sink and only רבא will be saved, leaving בר הדיא to drown.

keyTerms.meaning: Happens or is performed (said of a miracle)

phrases.english: He was going with him on a ship.
phrases.notes: בר הדיא was traveling with רבא.

phrases.english: He said: With a man
phrases.notes: בר הדיא is speaking to himself.

phrases.english: for whom a miracle happens — why do I need that?
phrases.notes: He fears a miracle where only רבא survives.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה קָא אָזֵיל בַּהֲדֵיהּ בְּאַרְבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows directly from the interpretation in step 31 that miracles would happen for רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בר הדיא fears being near רבא because the promised miracle might come at his own expense.

steps.title: A book falls and reveals the secret
steps.stepSummary: While boarding, בר הדיא drops a book. רבא finds it written there that all dreams follow the interpretation.
steps.simpleTranslation: As he was climbing up, a book fell from him. רבא found it and saw that it was written in it: 'All dreams follow the mouth.'
steps.whatsHappening: By accident, רבא finds בר הדיא's book. Inside is the rule that a dream comes true according to how it is interpreted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the turning point of the whole story. If dreams follow the interpretation, then בר הדיא's bad readings did not just predict רבא's troubles. They actually caused them. The גמרא taught this same principle earlier in the sugya.

keyTerms.meaning: All dreams follow the mouth: a dream's outcome follows its interpretation

steps.confusionAlert: בר הדיא was not just a fortune-teller who guessed right or wrong. According to this rule, his words actually decided what would happen. That is why רבא holds him responsible.
steps.whyThisMatters: This book reveals the hidden mechanism behind the whole story. It explains why רבא is so angry in the next step.

phrases.english: As he was climbing up
phrases.notes: בר הדיא was boarding the ship.

phrases.english: a book fell from him.
Rava found it and saw
that it was written in it
"All dreams follow the mouth."
phrases.notes: The outcome follows the interpreter's words.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּהֲדֵי דְּקָא סָלֵיק נְפַל סִיפְרָא מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the boat scene and reveals the key fact.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא discovers that dreams follow their interpretation, so בר הדיא controlled the outcomes.

steps.title: רבא rebukes and curses בר הדיא
steps.stepSummary: רבא calls בר הדיא wicked. He forgives everything except his wife's death, and he curses בר הדיא to fall into the hands of a merciless government.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Wicked one! It depended on you, and you caused me all this pain! I forgive you for all of it, except for the daughter of רב חסדא. May it be God's will that this man be handed over to a government that has no mercy on him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now understands that בר הדיא caused his troubles, and he reacts. He forgives most of it but curses בר הדיא over the death of his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא distinguishes between losses he can forgive and one he cannot: the death of his wife, the daughter of רב חסדא. Earlier on the daf, בר הדיא had given a reading predicting her death. The curse is specific, and the rest of the story will show it coming true.

phrases.english: He said: Wicked one,
it depended on you,
and you caused us so much pain!
I forgive you for all of them,
except for the daughter of Rav Chisda.
May it be the will that that man be handed over
into the hands of a government that has no mercy on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: רָשָׁע, בְּדִידָךְ קָיְימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא reacts to the discovery in the book.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא forgives everything except his wife's death, and curses בר הדיא to be handed over to a merciless kingdom.

steps.title: בר הדיא fears the curse and chooses exile
steps.stepSummary: בר הדיא knows that a sage's curse comes true, especially a justified one. He decides to go into exile so it will atone for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר הדיא said: What should I do? We have a tradition that a sage's curse comes true even when it is undeserved. All the more so with רבא, who cursed me justly. He said: I will get up and go into exile, for the Master said: Exile atones for sin.
steps.whatsHappening: בר הדיא panics about רבא's curse and looks for a way out. He decides to exile himself, hoping that exile will atone for his sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reasons with a כל שכן: if even an undeserved curse from a חכם comes true, a deserved one surely will. His plan is to use the principle that גלות atones for sin, hoping to cancel the curse.

keyTerms.meaning: A curse from a Torah sage

phrases.english: He said: What shall I do?
phrases.notes: בר הדיא is speaking to himself.

phrases.english: We have a tradition that a sage's curse,
even when undeserved, comes true,
and all the more so Rava,
who curses justly.
He said: I will get up and go into exile,
for the Master said: Exile atones for sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: מַאי אַעֲבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: בר הדיא responds to רבא's curse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sage's curse comes true even when undeserved, all the more so when deserved. בר הדיא chooses גלות as atonement.

steps.title: In Rome, the wardrobe keeper's first two dreams
steps.stepSummary: בר הדיא settles at the door of the king's chief wardrobe keeper. The keeper tells him two dreams, but each time he refuses to pay a זוז, so בר הדיא says nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He got up and went into exile to the Romans. He sat at the door of the king's chief wardrobe keeper. The keeper had a dream and said: I saw a needle go into my finger. בר הדיא said: Give me a זוז. He did not give it, so בר הדיא told him nothing. The keeper said: I saw a worm fall on my two fingers. בר הדיא said: Give me a זוז. He did not give it, and בר הדיא told him nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: בר הדיא carries out his exile and ends up in Rome. His old habit of interpreting only for money shows up again with the wardrobe keeper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is the same as with אביי and רבא earlier: no payment, no helpful interpretation. Here he says nothing at all. The dreams grow worse each time, from a needle in one finger to a worm on two fingers, building toward disaster.

keyTerms.meaning: The place of the Romans (the Roman government)
Chief keeper of the king's wardrobe

He went and sat at the entrance
of the king's chief wardrobe keeper.
The chief wardrobe keeper had a dream.
He said to him: I saw in a dream
that a needle went into my finger.
He said to him: Give me a zuz,
and he did not give it to him.
So he told him nothing at all.
He said to him: I saw that a worm fell
on my two fingers.
He said to him: Give me a zuz,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא יְהַב לֵיהּ, וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and he did not give it to him, so he did not tell him.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָם גְּלִי לְבֵי רוֹמָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the exile decided on in step 35.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בר הדיא again withholds his interpretation because he is not paid.

steps.title: The third dream and the ruin of the king's silks
steps.stepSummary: After the third dream, בר הדיא finally speaks: worms have eaten all the silk. The king hears of it, and the wardrobe keeper is about to be executed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The keeper said: I saw a worm fall on my whole hand. בר הדיא said: Worms have fallen on all the silk garments. The king's palace heard, and they brought the chief wardrobe keeper and were about to kill him.
steps.whatsHappening: With the third dream, בר הדיא gives an interpretation, but it is bad news: all the royal silk is ruined. The palace blames the wardrobe keeper and moves to execute him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worm grows from two fingers to the whole hand, and the damage spreads to all the silk. Because בר הדיא stayed silent earlier, the damage was never prevented. Now someone must pay with his life.

phrases.english: He said to him: I saw that a worm fell
on my whole hand.
He said to him: Worms have fallen
on all the silk garments.
phrases.notes: The king's silks have been eaten.

phrases.english: The king's palace heard,
and they brought the chief wardrobe keeper
and were about to execute him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזַאי דִּנְפַל תִּכְלָא בְּכוּלַּהּ יְדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of dreams to its disastrous result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The royal silks are ruined, and the wardrobe keeper faces execution.

steps.title: The blame shifts to בר הדיא
steps.stepSummary: The wardrobe keeper says the man who knew and stayed silent is to blame. They bring בר הדיא and accuse him: because of your זוז, the silks were ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: The keeper said to them: Why me? Bring this man, who knew and did not say. They brought בר הדיא and said to him: Because of your זוז, ruin came...
steps.whatsHappening: The wardrobe keeper defends himself by pointing at בר הדיא. The authorities bring בר הדיא and begin to accuse him. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now בר הדיא is in the hands of a merciless government, just as רבא's curse in step 34 said. His greed for a single זוז is named as the cause of the king's loss.

keyTerms.meaning: He knew and did not say

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's curse is coming true. בר הדיא's habit of interpreting only for money has delivered him to a merciless government.

phrases.english: He said to them: Why me?
Bring this one
who knew and did not say.
They brought bar Hadaya,
they said to him: Because of your zuz
were ruined...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud: the king's silks were ruined.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְהוּ: אֲנָא אַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The wardrobe keeper's defense turns the blame onto בר הדיא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בר הדיא is blamed because his demand for a זוז led to the ruin of the king's silks, fulfilling רבא's curse.
